solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Fabric obtained for ready money only

parts.note: ready money is cash in hand
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Someone buys a bolt of cloth and insists on paying in notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'obtained for' is just a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool fabric made from Kashmir goat hair.

clue.text: Dead man's chest

parts.note: a box that holds a corpse, playing on the pirate song about a dead man's chest

explanation.definitionFit: A coffin is the box a dead body is buried in, so it is the corpse's chest.

clue.text: In parts coastline is rocky

indicators.note: rocky means unstable or shaken, so the letters of coastline are jumbled

explanation.surface: In places the shore is covered in rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Sectional means made in or divided into separate sections or parts.

clue.text: Bike was blue

explanation.surface: A cyclist felt gloomy about the bicycle.
explanation.definitionFit: A moped is a low-powered motorbike, and moped is also the past tense of mope.

clue.text: Goes back after being fired

parts.note: a gun jerks backwards when it is shot, read as if a sacked worker were retreating

explanation.definitionFit: A gun recoils, kicking back when fired; to recoil is also to draw back.

clue.text: Rarely taken walk

parts.note: a little-used side path, a walk off the main route that few people take

explanation.definitionFit: A bypath is a secondary, unfrequented path, so it is a walk seldom used.

clue.text: Wild-eyed satyr of most recent history

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters of eyed satyr are shuffled

explanation.surface: A goggle-eyed mythical goat-man from the recent past.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday can mean the recent past, history that has only just happened.

clue.text: Factor eliminated by direct dealing

parts.note: a factor is a middleman, and dealing directly cuts out the middleman

explanation.definitionFit: An agent or factor acts for another person, and is bypassed when parties deal face to face.

clue.text: Centuries old political divisions

definitions.meaning: ... of runs in cricket, or a hundred years each
subdivisions of an English county in former times

explanation.surface: Ancient parliamentary splits lasting for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: A hundred was a historic subdivision of an English county.
explanation.definitionFit: Centuries are hundreds, and hundreds were also administrative divisions of old counties.

clue.text: Confront Wolves, say, in the mud

parts.note: to face someone is to confront them
wolves hunt in a pack; 'say' marks the pack of wolves as an example

explanation.surface: A football fan squares up to Wolves supporters on a muddy pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Wolves is also the nickname of Wolverhampton Wanderers football club, which makes the surface read as sport.
explanation.definitionFit: A beauty treatment of clay or mud spread over the face is called a face pack.

clue.text: A hard back for sailors

parts.note: stern means hard, severe

explanation.surface: A tough seafaring rear end, or a strict ship's discipline.
explanation.definitionFit: Astern is the nautical term for towards or at the back of a ship.

clue.text: A good man elevated to king and emperor

indicators.note: in a down clue, elevated means the pieces are lifted, read from bottom to top

parts.note: ST, saint, is the crossword good man
R is the abbreviation for king, from Latin rex

explanation.surface: A virtuous man is raised up to royalty and empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elevated' turns ST and A upward to give TSA before R; 'to' and 'and' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia before 1917.

clue.text: Classic appearing in 151AD

annotationWithheld.why: Classic appearing in 151AD: 151 in Roman numerals is CLI, so no reading of the figures gives ILI before AD; the setter seems to have meant 1, 50, 1 (I, L, I), which the printed number does not say.

clue.text: Official reformer of prison etc

indicators.note: a reformer remakes something, so the words that follow are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: A government official campaigns to reform prisons and similar institutions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reformer of' looks like a description of the official but signals rearranging PRISON ETC.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector is an official who examines and checks standards.

clue.text: They may be more than a touch unlucky for some batsmen

definitions.text: They may be more than a touch unlucky for some batsmen

parts.words: They may be more than a touch unlucky for some batsmen
parts.note: in cricket a faint edge off the bat can carry to the wicketkeeper and get the batsman out, a touch that proves unlucky

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, an edge is a ball that glances off the side of the bat.
explanation.definitionFit: Snicks are slight edges off a cricket bat, often caught behind for a dismissal.

clue.text: At chess I'd moved and switched

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted about, as pieces are on a chessboard

explanation.surface: During a game of chess I moved a piece and swapped it with another.
explanation.definitionFit: To be switched is to be beaten with a switch, a thin cane, so punished or chastised.

clue.text: Cleric angered about being screened

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes round the cleric

parts.note: riled means angered, irritated
DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a cleric

explanation.surface: A clergyman flies into a temper over being shown on television.
explanation.definitionFit: To riddle is to pass through a coarse sieve, so screened soil has been riddled.

clue.text: At length I made good — at the eleventh hour?

indicators.note: made good means repaired, so the letters of at length I are put right in a new order

explanation.surface: Eventually I succeeded, right at the last moment.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the eleventh hour is taken literally, as 11pm.
explanation.definitionFit: Eleven o'clock at night is literally late at night; the idiom means the last moment.

clue.text: Aircraft base advertises tour

parts.note: to air something is to make it public, advertise it
a trip is a tour or journey

explanation.surface: An airfield promotes its sightseeing trips.
explanation.definitionFit: An airstrip is a basic runway where aircraft take off and land.

clue.text: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy

definitions.text: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy

parts.words: The notoriety only a hypochondriac would enjoy
parts.note: a bad reputation read as a sickly kind of fame, which only someone who loves being unwell would relish

explanation.definitionFit: Ill fame means a bad reputation or notoriety; read literally it is fame for being sick.

clue.text: Be overthrown — that's bad

indicators.note: overthrown means turned over, so in a down clue the word is turned upside down

parts.note: to live is to be, exist

explanation.surface: Being toppled from power is a wicked thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Evil means wicked or very bad.

clue.text: Beast retiring with a broken toe

parts.note: coy means shy, retiring

indicators.note: broken means the letters of the word toe are smashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A shy animal limps away with an injured toe.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a wild dog of North America, a beast of prey.

clue.text: Brightened up when found not guilty

explanation.surface: A defendant cheers up on being acquitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleared describes the sky brightening and a person acquitted of a charge.

clue.text: Editorial boss

explanation.surface: The chief of a newspaper's opinion pages.
explanation.definitionFit: A leader is a newspaper editorial in British usage and also a person in charge.

clue.text: Game bird

definitions.meaning: a card game for one player, also a peg-board game
a large extinct flightless bird of Rodrigues island, and an American thrush

explanation.surface: A shooting party's quarry: a game bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire names both a one-player game and a kind of bird.

clue.text: Does he keep to the beaten track?

definitions.text: Does he keep to the beaten track?

parts.words: Does he keep to the beaten track?
parts.note: the beaten track is read as the course where someone is defeated, so it is where the defeated stay

explanation.definitionFit: A loser is someone who is beaten, as in a race, so the beaten track suits him.

clue.text: Criminal may be 21 down

definitions.meaning: a receiver of stolen goods is a criminal
a show-jumping obstacle may be cleared by a horse

explanation.surface: A suspect might get off scot-free.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is CLEARED, which the surface reads as acquitted but here means jumped over.
explanation.definitionFit: A fence is a dealer in stolen goods, and also a barrier that a horse may clear.

clue.text: Too delicate to use loud abuse

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical abbreviation for loud
to rail is to complain abusively

explanation.surface: Someone is too sensitive to shout insults.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to use' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Frail means weak and easily broken, too fragile to cope.

clue.text: Is among those left to fight

indicators.note: among means the word is goes inside the remainder

parts.note: the rest are those left over

explanation.surface: Some remain behind to take up arms.
explanation.definitionFit: To resist is to fight against or oppose.

clue.text: Fixed the score to suit the players

definitions.text: the score to suit the players
definitions.meaning: music adapted for particular instruments or voices

explanation.surface: A match was rigged so the players would be happy with the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Arranged means fixed in advance, and in music it means adapted for performers.

clue.text: Staff taken in by salary — it's a travesty

indicators.note: taken in by means the staff word sits inside the salary word

parts.note: pay is salary
a rod is a staff or stick

explanation.surface: Employees are swindled out of their wages, which is a scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: A parody is a mocking imitation, and a travesty is a grotesque imitation.

clue.text: One to perform afterwards for a devoted fan

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
to do is to perform
later means afterwards

explanation.surface: Someone takes the stage after the show for an adoring admirer.
explanation.definitionFit: An idolater worships someone or something excessively, like an ardent devotee.
